title: Useful math Tools
goal: This lesson covers a few handy tools: abs, round, min, max, and math.ceil / math.floor.
learn: Use abs, round, min, and max
idea: Python has built in helpers that do not need an import: abs() for absolute value, round(), min(), and max(). From the math module you also get math.ceil(x), which rounds up to the next whole number, and math.floor(x), which rounds down. These clean up messy numbers when you need whole counts or the biggest and smallest value.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change round(3.7) to round(3.2) and press Run. That line should print 3.

practice.text: Print the absolute value of -42 using abs().
practice.hint: abs() drops the minus sign and gives you the distance from zero. Put -42 inside abs().
practice.starterTip: Fill the print line with abs(-42). The output should be 42, not -42.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if abs(-42) is used and output is 42.

practice.text: Import math. Print math.ceil(7.2) and math.floor(7.2) on two lines.
practice.hint: ceil rounds up to the next whole number and floor rounds down. It is the same number with two different answers.
practice.starterTip: First print(math.ceil(7.2)) for 8, then print(math.floor(7.2)) for 7 on the next line.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if outputs are 8 and 7 using ceil and floor.

quiz.question: What does abs(-5) return?
quiz.correct: Right, abs removes the minus sign, so abs(-5) is 5.

quiz.question: What does math.ceil(2.1) return?
quiz.correct: Yes, ceil always rounds up, so 2.1 becomes 3.

quiz.question: What does max(3, 10, 7) return?
quiz.correct: Right, max picks the largest value, which is 10.
quiz.wrong: max gives you the biggest number in the group.
